strengths: Novel empirical finding that linear mode connectivity (LMC) holds across different SSL algorithms (MAE, MoCoV3, MMCR), demonstrated convincingly in Figure 2
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 ImageNet test distributions, LAION-C, and 21 VTAB datasets with 15 corruption types (336 test conditions total)
Clear presentation with effective visual communication and logical progression from basic soups to Self-Soupervision
Meaningful robustness improvements on distribution shifts (+3.5% ImageNet-C, +7% LAION-C when using shift-aware ingredients)
Good reproducibility with detailed training specifications in appendix, promised code release, and PyTorch example for Self-Seasoning
Fair comparison methodology using equal search/development costs (Figure 3) to compare against baselines
weaknesses: Largest reported gains (+3.5%/+7%) require access to test distribution for inter-training, which is unrealistic in deployment and inflates robustness claims—this undermines the practical significance of results
Modest gains in realistic scenarios: +1% on ImageNet-C, +0.4% on LAION-C, ~0.6% on VTAB transfer without test-set knowledge, without reported statistical significance

Unfair baseline comparison: 'continued SSL + supervised soup' baseline mixes from ONE SSL inter-training while Self-Soups search across M×N combinations; baselines should also search across multiple SSL algorithms for fair comparison
SSL Seasoning (§4.5) underperforms supervised alternatives on majority of tasks (only best on 4/21), undermining claims of effective unsupervised mixing
Many SSL hyperparameters noted as 'mostly chosen arbitrarily' (90% masking vs. standard 75%, 1 vs. 8 decoder layers)—unclear whether gains come from the method or fortunate hyperparameter selection
No theoretical explanation for why LMC holds with SSL ingredients; paper adds one case but doesn't advance understanding of the mechanism
Limited scope to vision domain and ViT-B architecture despite claims about SSL generality; only 3 of dozens of SSL algorithm families studied
Missing statistical significance testing and confidence intervals throughout; no ablation studies isolating method components
Incremental conceptual contribution: straightforward extension of Model Ratatouille (multi-stage training) by replacing supervised inter-training with SSL

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 experimental settings and 336 test conditions (21 VTAB tasks × 16 conditions), demonstrating thoroughness
Novel empirical finding that linear mode connectivity holds between ingredients differing in SSL algorithms—first demonstration of this phenomenon
Honest treatment of limitations, clearly stating that largest gains (+7%) require unlabeled target/shifted data and most gains are modest (≲1%)
Practical efficiency with no increased inference cost compared to single models
Good reproducibility effort with extensive implementation details in appendices
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: core contribution is straightforward combination of existing techniques (model soups + SSL inter-training). Authors acknowledge this is 'continued SSL + supervised soups,' a natural extension requiring no novel insights

Modest empirical gains in realistic scenarios: +1% on ImageNet-C, +0.4% on LAION-C in main setting (§4.2); no improvement on ImageNet-Val; ~1% on VTAB transfer. Largest gains (+7%) require impractical assumption of unlabeled test distribution data
No statistical significance testing: differences of 0.1-0.4% lack error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs. Results could easily be within noise
Self-Seasoning substantially underperforms supervised seasoning in Table 5, contradicting claims of competitiveness. Entropy minimization objective lacks theoretical justification
LMC finding lacks depth: unsurprising given prior work on supervised models, no theoretical analysis provided, empirical visualization (Figure 2) provides limited insight into underlying mechanisms
Missing computational cost analysis: no wall-clock time comparisons despite requiring M×N (3-4 × 4 = 12-16) training runs. Claims of 'equal search cost' to baselines not substantiated with numbers

Limited scope and generalizability: only 3 SSL algorithms tested despite acknowledging 'dozens of SSL algorithms absent.' Unclear whether findings generalize within families or are specific to these three

Weak analysis of when/why method works: no explanation for dramatically varying self-seasoning weights across tasks (0.98 vs. balanced); no ablations on ingredient count, training duration, or hyperparameter ranges; no analysis of algorithm complementarity

Experimental design concerns: different training regimes across experiments unexplained; mini-VTAB uses only 1K train/test samples (too small to be representative); hyperparameters described as 'arbitrary'; missing comparisons to domain adaptation methods beyond SAR

Presentation issues: cooking metaphor obscures clarity; terms like 'instant seasoning' vs. 'self-seasoning' easy to confuse; Figure 1 appears twice; Figure 2 visually clever but numerically hard to interpret; Table 4 extremely dense

strengths: Novel empirical finding: first demonstration that linear mode connectivity (LMC) holds between models trained with different SSL algorithms (MAE, MoCoV3, MMCR), supported by convincing visualization across 8 test sets (Figure 2)
Comprehensive and well-designed experiments across 5 distinct settings with proper baselines and fair cost comparisons; 336 test conditions for VTAB evaluation demonstrates thoroughness
Strong robustness results when unlabeled target data available: +3.5% on ImageNet-C and +7% on LAION-C; improvements persist with test-time adaptation
Excellent presentation with intuitive cooking metaphor, clear progression of ideas, detailed reproducibility information (Appendix B), and honest limitations discussion
Methodologically rigorous: proper distinction between Self-Soup and continued SSL baselines, careful handling of data splits (disjoint vs joint), equal search/development cost comparisons
weaknesses: Limited theoretical understanding: paper demonstrates LMC holds for SSL ingredients empirically but provides no explanation for why; lacks analysis of properties that preserve mode connectivity across algorithms

Modest practical improvements in most settings: ~0.1-0.4% gains on clean ImageNet (Table 1), <1% on VTAB transfer (Table 4), with some negative performance on noise corruption; largest gains (+7%) require access to unlabeled target distribution

Narrow evaluation scope: only 3 SSL algorithm families from dozens available; only Vision Transformers tested (CNN generalization unclear); restricted to image classification with no multimodal evaluation; acknowledgment that findings may only generalize within families

Missing key ablations and analysis: no investigation of whether all 3 SSL algorithms needed; limited characterization of which algorithm pairs are complementary; insufficient explanation of why inter-training on corrupted data helps; no sensitivity analysis for SSL hyperparameters (some chosen arbitrarily)

Statistical rigor issues: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs reported; small improvements (0.1-1%) lack significance testing, making it difficult to distinguish signal from noise; particularly concerning for extensive VTAB experiments

Self-Seasoning underperforms supervised alternatives: outperforms best ingredient on only 4/21 VTAB tasks (Table 5); entropy minimization objective appears somewhat ad-hoc; limited practical value when labeled data available

Computational cost underexplored: M×N development cost multiplier not clearly quantified; insufficient discussion of when this overhead is justified by modest improvements; limited practical applicability in resource-constrained settings

Limited technical novelty: core contribution is straightforward application of existing soups method to SSL; weight averaging and seasoning building on prior work; incremental over Model Soups baseline

strengths: Well-motivated and clearly presented work with excellent figures (especially Figure 1 and heatmaps in Figure 2) that effectively convey the core contributions through accessible soup metaphor
Comprehensive experimental validation across 336+ test conditions (21 VTAB tasks × 16 conditions) with proper controls including disjoint train/test splits for test-distribution scenarios
Novel empirical finding that linear mode connectivity holds between SSL-trained ingredients differing in algorithms and hyperparameters, extending known LMC cases from prior work
Extensive implementation details and reproducibility support (Appendix C with hyperparameters for all settings, promise to release code and mini-VTAB-C dataset)

Honest discussion of limitations clearly stating when gains are modest (~1%), when unlabeled test data is required for larger gains (+7%), and acknowledging that SSL hyperparameters were arbitrarily chosen
Practical versatility demonstrated across multiple scenarios: robustness to distribution shifts, transfer to 21 downstream tasks, and few-shot learning with Self-Seasoning
weaknesses: Modest practical gains on standard benchmarks limit impact: +0.9% on ImageNet-C/LAION-C vs. supervised soups, +1% average on VTAB, ~0% on clean ImageNet variants (Table 1)

Largest gains (+3.5% IN-C, +7% LAION-C) require inter-training on test distribution during training—a strong assumption that significantly limits real-world applicability despite controlled evaluation

Limited theoretical insight into why LMC holds for SSL ingredients; purely empirical observation based on 64 uniformly sampled convex combinations rather than rigorous verification across entire mixture space

Incremental novelty over Model Ratatouille: core contribution is using SSL instead of supervised inter-training for ingredient preparation; natural extension but not conceptually deep (Table 5 shows equivalent performance)

Insufficient ablations and sensitivity analysis: SSL hyperparameters noted as 'mostly chosen arbitrarily' with no systematic study of robustness to these choices, number of inter-trainings, or hyperparameter sensitivity

Missing important practical comparisons: no wall-clock time overhead analysis despite requiring 16-24+ full training runs, limited comparison to other robustness methods and recent model merging approaches, no multi-run error bars or significance testing
Self-Seasoning methodology somewhat ad-hoc (entropy minimization via kNN predictions) without ablations comparing alternative unsupervised objectives or justification for this particular choice
Evaluation limited to vision/image classification; no validation on other modalities (language, multimodal) where SSL is common, limiting generalizability claims
Only 4 SSL methods tested despite acknowledgment that 'dozens of SSL algorithms' exist; generalization to other algorithm families and parameter regimes unclear

strengths: Clear presentation with effective use of metaphor and strong figure quality
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse benchmarks (ImageNet variants, LAION-C, VTAB-21) with detailed hyperparameter specifications
First empirical demonstration that linear mode connectivity holds between SSL ingredients with different algorithms across 8 test sets
Honest discussion of limitations and strong reproducibility support with promised code/data
Practical efficiency: no inference cost increase while leveraging unlabeled data
weaknesses: Marginal empirical improvements in primary scenarios: <1% gains on ImageNet/VTAB clean data, undermining the practical value for practitioners

Unfair comparisons in Section 4.3: largest improvements (+3.5%, +7%) leverage test-distribution information that baselines don't access, making gains somewhat circular rather than demonstrating method superiority
Limited novelty: straightforward combination of existing techniques (different SSL algorithms → standard model soups); Self-Seasoning is simply kNN entropy minimization without novelty
Lack of theoretical insight into why LMC holds for SSL ingredients or when it might fail; demonstration limited to single architecture, one stock, and four algorithms
Missing critical ablations: no sensitivity analysis for SSL training duration, no justification for arbitrary SSL hyperparameters, no comparison of computational cost vs. alternatives
Weak experimental controls: 'equal search cost' framing doesn't hold when comparing M×N SSL runs vs. M×N supervised runs—baselines match performance on clean data (Table 1)
Insufficient analysis of SSL algorithm complementarity beyond observing empirical LMC; learned mixture coefficients (Table 8) are presented without interpretable insights
VTAB corruption experiments use artificial ImageNet-C overlays on unrelated domains, potentially unrepresentative of natural distribution shifts

strengths: First demonstration that linear mode connectivity holds across ingredients trained with different SSL algorithms—a novel and surprising finding that enables new model soup variants

Exceptionally comprehensive experimental evaluation across 336 test conditions (21 VTAB datasets with 15 corruptions each, plus ImageNet variants), demonstrating thoroughness and reproducibility commitment
Strong practical gains in targeted scenarios: +7% on LAION-C and +3.5% on ImageNet-C when inter-training on corrupted test distributions, with zero inference cost overhead
Novel Self-Seasoning method for unsupervised mixture weighting using kNN entropy minimization, enabling soups without task-specific labels
Careful experimental design with proper baselines (including 'continued SSL + supervised soups' with equal search/development cost) and honest treatment of limitations
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (especially Figure 2 mixture heatmaps) and reproducible setup details in appendices
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: primarily combines two existing techniques (SSL + model soups) without introducing fundamentally new principles; Equations 2-3 are relatively straightforward applications
Modest gains in standard deployment scenarios: only +0.29% on ImageNet-Val, +1% on VTAB natural tasks—within noise margins without statistical significance testing or confidence intervals

Missing ablation studies and mechanistic analysis: no explanation for why LMC holds across fundamentally different SSL algorithms (MAE, contrastive, dimension-contrastive); arbitrary hyperparameter choices claimed as robust without systematic evidence

Suspicious test-set inter-training results: identical performance in 'disjoint' (35.72%) vs. 'joint' (36.02%) settings on ImageNet-C suggests minimal benefit from holding out test samples, raising concerns about what drives the gains
Inconsistent transfer learning results: Self-Souping shows +1.4% on natural tasks but -1% on noise corruptions with no clear patterns explaining when the method helps
Limited scope: only 4 SSL algorithms tested (acknowledged 'dozens' exist), single architecture (ViT-B with one validation), vision-only evaluation, so generalization claims are unvalidated
Computational cost underspecified: developing M×N ingredients substantially increases training cost over supervised soups; trade-off analysis between development and deployment costs missing
Self-Seasoning evaluation incomplete: only tested in few-shot VTAB setting; results roughly tied with labeled seasoning, undermining claims of unsupervised advantage
